The protein is most likely **aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase** (EC 1.2.1.11), an enzyme in aspartate-family amino-acid biosynthesis.

It likely uses NADPH to convert **L-aspartyl-4-phosphate** into **L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde**. This intermediate feeds into the biosynthesis of **lysine** via the diaminopimelate pathway, as well as **methionine** and **threonine**.

This assignment is supported by 66.7–68.2% sequence identity across nearly the full length to reviewed enzyme homologs, and matches to the enzyme’s two characteristic Pfam domains. It is a strong sequence-based inference, not direct experimental confirmation for the supplied protein.
